camera.position: resting low on a mossy boulder at the edge of a muddy forest path, about ten meters from the path, looking across it side-on at the height of a person's knee
camera.framing: the muddy path runs from the left background diagonally across the frame to the right midground, where it passes through a narrow gap between two massive dawn redwood trunks; the juvenile Triceratops carrying Nora is in the center-left midground, side-on to the view; the tyrannosaur is in the left background on the same path; the frame does not move, pan or zoom

setting.location: Hell Creek floodplain forest, Montana, Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago, warm humid late morning
elements: a humid riverside forest of broadleaf flowering trees and shrubs mixed with tall straight dawn redwood trunks; hazy sunlight slants in from the upper left; low ferns and leafy shrubs line both sides of the path, no grass anywhere; the path is soft wet mud with puddles; warm and humid, no snow, no frost, no winter

two massive dawn redwood trunks stand close together on the right side of the path from frame 0; the gap between them is wide enough for the Triceratops but much narrower than the tyrannosaur's body; they stay in that spot for the whole clip
exactly two dinosaurs and one person in the whole clip, all visible from frame 0; no other animals, no birds in the frame, no other people; nothing appears from nowhere and nothing vanishes

characters.name: Nora
characters.visual_lock: matches the Nora Body reference image exactly for her build and clothing; honey-blonde hair tied in a high ponytail at the crown of her head, with wispy curtain bangs parted in the middle; fair skin
characters.outfit: wears the exact historical outfit shown in the Nora Body reference sheet: golden-tan deer suede tunic with long sleeves that reach all the way to her wrists (never sleeveless), wide dark belt, golden-tan suede leggings the same color as the tunic that cover her legs completely from hips to boots, and criss-cross laced knee boots; no bare skin on her thighs, knees or shins at any moment (NO shearling collar, NO extra fur, NO hood, NO fringe, NO tassels, NO outfit variations)
characters.action: rides astride the Triceratops just behind its frill, leaning forward low over its neck; for the whole clip both her hands grip the rim of the frill and never let go, even while she talks; her knees clamp the Triceratops's flanks and her boots hang along its ribs; her face is turned three-quarters toward the view whenever she speaks, so her mouth stays visible

characters.name: Juvenile Triceratops
characters.visual_lock: matches the Juvenile Triceratops reference image exactly: pony-sized, olive-brown pebbly hide with darker mottled bands, short backward-curving brow horns, short rounded frill
characters.position: galloping heavily from left to right along the path with Nora on its back; with Nora seated on it, her head is lower than the tyrannosaur's thigh

characters.name: Tyrannosaur
characters.visual_lock: matches the Tyrannosaurus reference image exactly: massive boxy skull, tiny two-fingered forearms, dark grey-brown pebbly hide, tail held straight out
characters.position: striding along the same path behind them, from the left background toward the right; more than twice as tall as the Triceratops: its hips are higher than the Triceratops's frill with Nora on top; it moves at a heavy fast walk, never a sprint, one foot always on the ground

timeline_action.0-3s: From frame 0 the Triceratops is already galloping left to right in the center-left midground with Nora low on its back, and the tyrannosaur is already striding about twenty-five meters behind them at a heavy fast walk in the left background. The Triceratops's short legs pump hard; its belly skin sways and its frill and head bob with every stride. Nora shouts from second 0, her face three-quarters toward the view.
timeline_action.3-7s: The tyrannosaur closes to about ten meters with long heavy strides. From about 3.5 to 5 seconds it lifts its head and opens its jaws wide in one long roar while Nora goes silent and presses herself low against the frill; its jaws close again by 5 seconds. Then Nora shouts again. The Triceratops reaches the two trunks on the right.
timeline_action.7-10s: The Triceratops squeezes through the gap between the two trunks and slows to a heavy trot just beyond them, still inside the right edge of the frame, and Nora turns her head back toward the tyrannosaur, laughing. The tyrannosaur plants both feet and skids in the mud a body length before the trunks, its body lurching forward past its feet and its tail swinging up as a counterweight, then settles to a stop without touching the trunks; it turns its head slowly from side to side over about one second, no sudden snap. Nora finishes her line by about 9 seconds; the last half second is the tyrannosaur standing still, chest heaving.

motion_choreography.frame0_state: Static side-on view across the muddy path; the Triceratops with Nora riding low is mid-gallop in the center-left midground, all four of its feet visible; the tyrannosaur is mid-stride in the left background, about twenty-five meters behind; the two close trunks stand on the right side of the path; the gap between them is empty.

0-3s.Nora: both hands gripping the frill rim; leaning forward low; knees clamping the flanks; her ponytail bounces a beat behind each stride; shouting toward the view in three-quarter profile
0-3s.Juvenile Triceratops: heavy gallop, legs pumping in a fast rhythm, each foot slapping into the mud and throwing a spray of mud behind it; belly skin sways; head and frill bob with each stride
0-3s.Tyrannosaur: a heavy fast walk, never a run: one foot is always on the ground, never both feet in the air; the body dips and rises with every step, huge thigh muscles bunch and the thigh skin ripples on each impact, the tail swings slightly against each stride, head held level and forward, mouth closed with its scaly lips covering the teeth

3-7s.Nora: both hands still gripping the frill rim; during the roar she flattens herself against the frill, eyes squeezed shut, silent; then she lifts her head and shouts toward the view
3-7s.Juvenile Triceratops: keeps galloping toward the trunks, breath snorting, mud flying
3-7s.Tyrannosaur: closes in; at 3.5 seconds its head rises and its jaws open wide for one long roar, neck muscles straining, closing by 5 seconds; keeps striding at a heavy fast walk

7-10s.Nora: both hands still gripping the frill rim; turns her head back over her shoulder toward the tyrannosaur, laughing with relief, mouth visible
7-10s.Juvenile Triceratops: squeezes between the trunks without touching them, then slows to a heavy trot just beyond, still in the right edge of the frame, flanks heaving
7-10s.Tyrannosaur: plants both feet and skids, two deep furrows ploughing through the mud, body lurches forward and settles, tail swings up and settles a beat later; stops a body length before the trunks; chest heaves; head turns slowly side to side

motion_choreography.end_state: The Triceratops with Nora stands just beyond the trunks at the right edge of the frame, flanks heaving; the tyrannosaur stands stopped a body length before the trunks on the left side of the gap, chest heaving; the two animals are separated by the trunks and never touch.

speech.speaker: Nora
speech.voice_profile: Laomedeia, breathless and panicked, rising into a cracking shout in danger, then a relieved laugh

segments.0-3s: Go, go, go! Big guy, faster, please!
segments.3-7s: That's a tyrannosaur, it's right behind us!
segments.7-10s: Through the gap, squeeze! Yes! It's too big to fit!

delivery.0-3s: Nora shouts (breathless, urgent, bouncing with each stride)
delivery.3-7s: Nora stays silent during the roar, then shouts (panicked, high and cracking)
delivery.7-10s: Nora shouts (breaking into a relieved laugh)

speech.dialogue: Go, go, go! Big guy, faster, please! That's a tyrannosaur, it's right behind us! Through the gap, squeeze! Yes! It's too big to fit!

audio.ambience: forest air and insects, low under her voice
audio.sfx: heavy thudding footfalls and mud splashes from both animals, low under her voice; one long deep tyrannosaur roar from 3.5 to 5 seconds while Nora is silent

physical_realism.force_and_traction: both animals are enormously heavy: every footfall sinks deep into the wet mud and throws mud and water sideways; the tyrannosaur's footfalls make the nearby ferns tremble; its skid ploughs two deep furrows and pushes a wave of mud ahead of its feet; the Triceratops's hooves slap and suck out of the mud; the tyrannosaur cannot stop quickly: its skid takes two full strides
physical_realism.secondary_motion: thigh and belly skin of both animals ripple and sway on each impact; the tyrannosaur's tail swings against its stride and settles a beat after it stops; Nora's ponytail bounces a beat behind each stride; fern fronds whip aside as the animals pass and spring back
physical_realism.environment: hazy sunbeams between the trees, flying mud droplets catching the light, muddy water rippling in the puddles after each footfall
physical_realism.camera_response: the frame stays fixed; it shakes slightly with each heavy tyrannosaur footfall as the ground vibrates, then steadies
physical_realism.documentary_texture: matte, dry, weathered scaly hides caked with real mud, real contact shadows under the animals' bellies and feet, natural available light only, slight motion blur on the fast legs; looks like real wildlife documentary footage of living animals, not CGI, not a game, not toys, not animatronics

negative_constraints: the view never moves, pans or zooms; nobody touches it; the camera lens and viewpoint are completely outside the visible frame and never seen
the tyrannosaur never touches, bites or catches the Triceratops or Nora, and never touches the trunks; the two animals never touch
the tyrannosaur never comes toward the view; it strides from left to right along the path
Nora stays seated on the Triceratops for the whole clip and never falls; both her hands stay on the frill rim
exactly two dinosaurs and one person; no other animals and no other people
the two dinosaurs are separate bodies; they never overlap or merge
no snow, no frost, no winter
no subtitles, no text on screen, no watermark
no morphing or vanishing animals, people or objects
no metal, no modern items anywhere in the frame
the animals look like real heavy living animals, never like plastic toys, rubber models or animatronics
the tyrannosaur never leaps and never has both feet off the ground; its teeth show only while its jaws are open for the roar
